label: input token f at one of the first three original positions
explanation: Fires only when the input token is the letter f and only in the original phase. It never fires on any other token, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase (even when f is fed back in as an input). Firing is limited to early positions: t=0, 1, 2 fire at about the same rate (about a third of f inputs at each), t=3 rarely and weakly (0.5% of mass), and t>=4 never. Magnitude falls with position: f at t=0 gives the maximum (1.87), and t=1 and t=2 give smaller values (activation mass shares 0.43 / 0.36 / 0.21 on similar step counts). A repeated f still fires (e.g. f f p gives 1.00 then 0.86). The only misses are the weak t=3 activations.

issues: The explanation gets the firing rate wrong. It says t=0, 1 and 2 each fire on 'about a third of f inputs', but the feature fires on essentially every original-phase f at t<=2. On the test split, the predicate (phase==0)&(in_tok==f)&(t==0) has precision 1.000 (16729 predicted, all active), and the full t<=2 predicate has 0 false positives. The 'one third' figure is each position's share of the active steps (recall 0.31 for t==0), not the share of f inputs that fire.

Everything else checks out. In the dev profile, the delimiter and copy phases have 0 active steps, every token other than f has 0 active steps, and t>=4 has 0 active steps. Activation mass shares by t are 0.431 / 0.358 / 0.207 / 0.005 and the max is 1.868, matching the explanation.

At t=3 the feature fires on about 22% of f inputs, and only weakly. The t==3 predicate has precision 0.224 and mass recall 0.0045, and all of its coverage is in the lowest activation quartile. Test-split misses are all weak t=3 f activations (0.00-0.10 relative to max). That is a small tail, not a systematic gap. Adding t=3 drops F1 to 0.896 (precision 0.81), so the original predicate is the better one.
The label matches the predicate and does not overclaim. Test scores reproduce: precision 1.000, recall 0.933, F1 0.965.
